summary.name: Claymation (supplemental reference, category Animation Techniques). The source collection does not name it directly, so it is not a confirmed collection style.
summary.visualIdentity: Matte sculpted clay with soft handmade lumps, small fingerprints and credible contact between parts. Shapes change as if physically adjusted between exposures, under stable light. Avoid liquid-like flow and glossy plastic sheen. Digital clay-like renders must be labeled as simulations.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: character craft pieces and playful character-led shorts, per the source's combination guidance. Explicitly compatible: the clay-specific 360° orbit of a finished hero (motion-043) and the camera orbit (motion-021). Inferred: short sculpted-character explainers. Other uses are unspecified.
summary.limitations: No listed renderer exists. Authentic output needs photographed clay; otherwise a Blender clay simulation must be labeled as such, and simulated physics is not validated. Full orbits need finished geometry on every side, so flat or 2.5D art cannot support them. The source review covered only sampled seconds 1–8, with no audio or later scenes.
summary.palette: The background policy is scene_dependent: choose it from subject, environment, lighting and mood. The example tokens (#F0E4D3 background, #444B3D foreground, #A2A680 and #C58D74 accents) are unapproved suggestions. Foreground on background measures 7.218. Both accents fail the 4.5 body-text target, so they are decorative only. Gradients are disabled. Task-provided exact colors override these tokens.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Pose changes follow a planned exposure cadence with held states. Do not add automatic in-betweens, springs or bounce. Optional motion references are candidates only: motion-006 bounded pupil gaze needs eye layers, motion-009 layered parallax needs separated depth layers, motion-010 and motion-043 are orbits, and motion-012 and motion-015 structure chapters. Choose none if the scene does not support the action. Pointer and scroll apply only to interactive delivery.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified in the source. Without user audio, a proposed direction is silence or soft ambience, optionally with restrained music chosen for the topic. Speech is optional voiceover. Sung vocals are unspecified. Do not claim beat or speech sync without measured data.
summary.assetRequirements: Assets are optional, and none were supplied. Photographed clay needs numbered frame sequences with alpha, consistent dimensions and a layer manifest. A Blender route needs clay materials labeled as simulation. Gaze needs eye layers or a rig. A full orbit needs complete geometry or a stated turntable view count. Parallax needs layered art with crop margins. Local fonts must load before rendering.
summary.combinations: style-115 (reaction captions): use outlined text in the foreground color, with at most two accents, stepping on the clay exposure cadence and clear of faces. Avoid glossy caption effects. style-105 (music-led promos): align pose holds to a verified beat table, without a change on every beat. Captions stay as separate DOM text layers.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline. It uses data-composition-id, clip timing, and one paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines, followed by check, snapshot and render. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists. Photographed frames or Blender are the style renderer, and GSAP owns motion. Three.js is for true 3D, PixiJS for 2D, and chroma-js for palette checks. FFmpeg assembles frames and audio. Verify seeks and decoded frames.
